**3B.4 Research Note: Vladimir Putin in 2024**

Bottom line: the 2024 record is **strongly against**. I found only one weak procedural-safety decree, but no credible evidence of real due process, civilian oversight, or independent investigation of abuse. The public record instead shows a system that tolerated or embedded abusive punishment.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Slightly for 3B.4, but indirect | `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 01.03.2024 г. № 162` | Kremlin | 2024-03-01 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print | Putin amended military statutes to require commanders to prevent crimes and incidents, report problems promptly, and respond to weapons-storage alarms. This is the only 2024 item that weakly points toward oversight or discipline, but it is broad governance rather than due process or independent abuse review. | 3B.4, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Against 3B.4 | `Russia: Prisoner of conscience Aleksei Navalny, Kremlin’s most vocal opponent, dies in custody` | Amnesty International | 2024-02-16 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/russia-prisoner-of-conscience-aleksei-navalny-kremlins-most-vocal-opponent-dies-in-custody/ | Amnesty says Navalny was poisoned, unjustly imprisoned, and tortured before dying in custody. This is strong evidence against independent accountability mechanisms for politically protected abuse. | 3B.4, 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Against 3B.4 | `Russia: Authorities punishing imprisoned anti-war critics and dissenters by denying family contact` | Amnesty International | 2024-06-26 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/russia-authorities-punishing-imprisoned-anti-war-critics-and-dissenters-by-denying-family-contact/ | Amnesty says authorities systematically denied family contact to imprisoned critics through legal loopholes and fabricated pretexts. That points to punitive abuse with no meaningful complaint-handling or due-process correction. | 3B.4, 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Against 3B.4 | `Russian Federation: Further Information: Prosecution of Imprisoned Ukrainian Continues: Oleksandr Marchenko` | Amnesty International | 2024-02-16 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/eur46/7725/2024/en/ | Amnesty reports that Marchenko was repeatedly placed in punishment cells on spurious grounds and denied urgent health care. This indicates tolerated custodial abuse, not independent oversight. | 3B.4, 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Against 3B.4 | `Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report` | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says the Kremlin intensified restrictions, used fabricated criminal cases, and detainees were frequently abused during or after arrest. This is evidence against due process and against complaint systems that restrain abuse. | 3B.4, 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Against 3B.4 | `Russia: Nations in Transit 2024 Country Report` | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024 | Freedom House reports political persecution, harsh prison conditions, and abuse in pretrial detention centers, alongside a large antiwar prosecution wave. That is systemic abuse, not independent investigation of it. | 3B.4, 3B.2, 3B.1 |

**Synthesis**

- Best-supported conclusion: **No**.
- The only pro-side evidence is a broad discipline decree; it does not amount to due process, complaint handling, civilian oversight, or independent abuse investigation.
- The stronger pattern is repeated abuse of political prisoners, detainees, and critics, with no sign of effective institutional correction.
- Search gap: I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that Putin built independent civilian oversight bodies, complaint channels, or meaningful internal investigations for abuse by politically protected actors.
